context.why: The last story, and it closes the loop. An upload from a Data Assessor waits for a Data Curator. Curators see what is waiting, open one, and either approve it — which makes the dataset public — or send it back with a comment saying what is wrong, which returns it to its uploader for a replacement file. You also carry T029, moved here from the previous story: setting a dataset public on a curator's own confirmation. It belongs beside the approval action because both make a dataset public by the same mechanism, and the previous story could not complete it for a reason recorded as D27.
context.environment: Python 3.13 via Poetry, virtualenv already synced. Prefix commands with `poetry run`. Tests: `poetry run pytest`. Lint gate: `poetry run pre-commit run -a`, never raw ruff. A development server is already running from this worktree on 0.0.0.0:8001 with the autoreloader; do not start another and do not stop it.
spec_sections: spec.md User Story 6 and its six acceptance scenarios
prior_decisions: D27, and read it before writing any visibility code: public means Dataset.visibility = Visibility.PUBLIC and NOTHING ELSE on the framework version this project resolves. Dataset.published exists on the framework's development branch and DOES NOT EXIST here. Verify against the installed package in the virtualenv, never against ~/projects/fairdm — they share a version number and carry different code.
The default manager already excludes private datasets, so the private guarantee holds with the one field.
Private is the default. Never write code that sets a dataset private — the safe outcome must be what happens when no code runs.
D2: the role is the trust level. A curator's own upload does not wait. An assessor's does. No per-person flag.

D8: no notification framework. FR-022 is met by the navigation entry's count of assessments awaiting a decision, which US-1 already built, plus the queue you are building. Do not add a dependency, a model or email.
D7: every submitted file is kept. A send-back does not delete the data already imported into the private dataset; the replacement imports over it.
Transitions live in review.states and enforce who may make them. Do not re-implement the rule in a view.
D16/#367: the DEBUG=False chrome defect is upstream and not yours.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given a checked file, When a Data Curator confirms it, Then the dataset's visibility is set to public and the assessment reaches COMPLETE; and When a Data Assessor confirms, Then visibility is not written, the dataset stays private and the assessment moves to AWAITING_DECISION. Prove the public branch fails if the visibility write is removed.

Given assessments in AWAITING_DECISION, When a Data Curator views the queue, Then each appears naming its publication and who uploaded it; and When a Data Assessor requests the same URL, Then it is refused.
Given a waiting assessment, When a curator approves it, Then the dataset becomes public, the assessment reaches COMPLETE, and decided_by and decided_at are recorded.

Given a waiting assessment, When a curator sends it back with a comment, Then the dataset stays private, the comment is recorded and shown to the uploader, the assessment moves to CHANGES_REQUESTED, and a replacement file can be uploaded and confirmed, returning it to AWAITING_DECISION.
Given an assessment awaiting a decision, When anyone who is not a Data Curator attempts to approve it — including the Data Assessor who uploaded it — Then it is refused.
Given the queue and decision routes, When they are reached by their URL names, Then they resolve, render for a curator, and refuse everyone else.
